nodes.summary: If popping the back of a deque $d$ succeeds and returns an element $x$ and a deque $d'$, then the sequence represented by $d$ is the sequence represented by $d'$ followed by $x$.
nodes.title: Popping the back of a deque

nodes.summary: If popping the front of a deque $d$ succeeds and returns an element $x$ and a deque $d'$, then the sequence represented by $d$ is $x$ followed by the sequence represented by $d'$.
nodes.title: Popping the front of a deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$ and element $x$, the sequence represented by the deque obtained by pushing $x$ at the back of $d$ is the sequence represented by $d$ followed by $x$.
nodes.title: Pushing at the back of a deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$ and element $x$, the sequence represented by the deque obtained by pushing $x$ at the front of $d$ is $x$ followed by the sequence represented by $d$.
nodes.title: Pushing at the front of a deque

nodes.summary: The sequence represented by a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$ is $f$ followed by the reverse of $b$; it lists the elements from front to back.
nodes.title: Represented sequence of a deque

nodes.summary: A deque with elements in a type $\alpha$ consists of two lists of elements of $\alpha$, the front list and the back list. The front list holds the front part of the sequence in order and the back list holds the back part in reverse order.
nodes.title: Two-list deque

nodes.summary: The empty deque is the deque whose front list and back list are both empty.
nodes.title: The empty deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$, the emptiness test of $d$ returns true if and only if the sequence represented by $d$ is empty.
nodes.title: Correctness of the deque emptiness test

nodes.summary: The emptiness test of a deque returns true exactly when both its front list and its back list are empty.
nodes.title: Emptiness test for a deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$, peeking at the back of $d$ returns the last element of the sequence represented by $d$ when that sequence is nonempty, and returns nothing when it is empty.
nodes.title: Peeking at the back of a deque

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$, where $b$ is stored in reverse order. Peeking at the back of $d$ returns, without removing it, the first element of $b$ when $b$ is nonempty, and otherwise the last element of $f$; when both lists are empty it returns no element.
nodes.title: Peek at the back of a deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$, peeking at the front of $d$ returns the first element of the sequence represented by $d$, and returns no element when that sequence is empty.
nodes.title: Peeking at the front gives the first element

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$, where $b$ is stored in reverse order. Peeking at the front of $d$ returns, without removing it, the first element of $f$ when $f$ is nonempty, and otherwise the last element of $b$; when both lists are empty it returns no element.
nodes.title: Peek at the front of a deque

nodes.summary: For every deque $d$, popping the back of $d$ returns no result if and only if the sequence represented by $d$ is empty.
nodes.title: Popping the back fails exactly on empty deques

If $b$ has first element $v$ and remaining list $b'$, popping the back of $d$ returns $v$ together with the deque with front list $f$ and back list $b'$. nodes.summary: For every deque $d$, popping the front of $d$ returns no result if and only if the sequence represented by $d$ is empty.
nodes.title: Popping the front fails exactly on empty deques

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$, where $b$ is stored in reverse order. If $f$ has first element $v$ and remaining list $f'$, popping the front of $d$ returns $v$ together with the deque with front list $f'$ and back list $b$. nodes.title: Pop the front of a deque

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$, where $b$ is stored in reverse order. Pushing an element $x$ at the back of $d$ gives the deque with front list $f$ and back list consisting of $x$ followed by the entries of $b$.
nodes.title: Push at the back of a deque

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a deque with front list $f$ and back list $b$, where $b$ is stored in reverse order. Pushing an element $x$ at the front of $d$ gives the deque with front list consisting of $x$ followed by the entries of $f$, and back list $b$.
nodes.title: Push at the front of a deque

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.

breadcrumbs.label: Lists, stacks, queues and dynamic arrays
